SHORT REFLECTION

What the data supports—and what it cannot prove

What we can learn

This project supports descriptive comparisons of recorded national tourism activity. The clearest example is seasonal concentration: in 2024, the two busiest months accounted for 55.9% of accommodation nights in Croatia, 36.0% in France and 24.3% in Germany. Those differences help planners identify questions about campaign timing. Receipts and accommodation measures add context about scale, while explicit coverage gaps show where more research is needed.

What remains unproven

These patterns do not prove that tourism causes local congestion or that a campaign would improve community wellbeing. A national bed-place total does not establish rooms available in a particular city. Travel receipts are neither profit nor spending per visitor. Airline activity cannot establish useful transport connections. Canada’s resident response cannot represent communities elsewhere, and missing feedback cannot be interpreted as approval.

How the project’s choices shape its conclusions

Reusing an energy-based country sample makes the dataset convenient but gives it a selection bias toward large economies. Monthly data cover only three European countries, so even the strongest seasonal comparison has limited reach. Arrival definitions and reporting years vary. These constraints mean that rankings should prompt investigation rather than declare winners. Preserving blanks is more honest than filling them with plausible guesses.

What should happen next

A tourism board could investigate a small campaign in a locally verified quieter period, after checking accommodation, attractions, transport and published aggregate resident evidence. Evaluation should compare compatible local measures over time and account for events, weather and other influences; a before-and-after change alone would not establish causation. The site’s value is in making these decisions more transparent, including when the evidence is insufficient to act.

Evidence: Eurostat monthly nights, 2024 · Definitions, sources and limitations · Country records. Reflection on the 20 September 2026 release.
